source.note: Domain and task titles are preserved from the embedded app-data package. Study targets are app-authored paraphrased learning targets, not verbatim BRPT blueprint wording.

tasks.title: Patient information and clinical assessment
tasks.focus: Know the patient's reason for testing, symptoms, risk factors, medications, and baseline clinical picture before the study begins.
studyTargets: Review why the patient is being tested and what disorder is suspected.
Know common symptoms tied to OSA, CSA, hypersomnolence, circadian disorders, parasomnias, and movement disorders.
Watch for medication effects, comorbidities, safety concerns, and age-specific issues.
Think in diagnostic groups: breathing disorders, hypersomnolence, circadian disorders, parasomnias, and movement disorders.
Be able to distinguish adult vs pediatric clues when the same disorder can present differently.
tasks.nextAction: Review clinical intake clues, then practice order/indication, history, medication, and sleep-disorder recognition items.

tasks.title: Patient and caregiver education
tasks.focus: Explain the study clearly, reduce anxiety, set expectations, and give patient-centered instructions before lights out and before discharge.
studyTargets: Explain hookup, sensors, room setup, and why signal quality matters.
Teach simple pre-study and post-study expectations in plain language.
Use age-appropriate teaching for pediatric patients and caregivers.
Reinforce safety, comfort, and what to do during the night if help is needed.
Support adherence by making instructions clear, calm, and realistic.
tasks.nextAction: Study patient-facing explanations first, then practice calm education and caregiver-support scenarios.

tasks.title: Provide therapy support
tasks.focus: Support tolerance, comfort, and early success with PAP, oxygen, or other prescribed therapy-related needs.
studyTargets: Recognize barriers like claustrophobia, poor fit, leaks, dryness, fear, and confusion.
Coach mask/interface comfort and explain what normal adjustment feels like.
Know when to escalate concerns to the provider or follow center protocol.
Use supportive language that improves acceptance and adherence.
Document patient response and any tolerance issues clearly.
tasks.nextAction: Focus on PAP comfort, desensitization, adherence support, download basics, and when to redirect to the clinical team.

tasks.title: Determine technical preparation
tasks.focus: Choose the correct setup, sensors, calibrations, and monitoring approach for the ordered study and the patient's clinical needs.
studyTargets: Know standard PSG, PAP titration, split-night, MSLT, MWT, HSAT, and pediatric setup differences.
Use the right channels, backup supplies, and special sensors when clinically indicated.
Match the setup to the order, symptoms, age group, and safety needs.
Think ahead about CO2 monitoring, oxygen, seizure precautions, or mobility issues when appropriate.
Confirm the study plan before hookup so the night does not drift off course.
tasks.nextAction: Review setup, sensors, electrode placement, filters, sampling, impedance, and standard precautions.

tasks.title: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
tasks.focus: Run the ordered study correctly from hookup through lights on while staying within guideline-based technologist practice.
studyTargets: Perform calibrations, biocals, signal checks, and troubleshooting methodically.
Follow study-specific workflow for PSG, PAP titration, MSLT, MWT, or HSAT support.
Use current standards for sensor use, monitoring, and study conduct.
Document key events, interventions, and technical issues as they happen.
Stay consistent so the final record is interpretable and defensible.
tasks.nextAction: Practice the study workflow: PSG, pediatric PSG, MSLT/MWT, HSAT, safety, and documentation steps.

tasks.title: Identify, respond, and document
tasks.focus: Recognize clinically important changes during the study and respond safely while documenting what happened and what you did.
studyTargets: Identify artifact, lead loss, respiratory events, rhythm concerns, behavioral events, and safety issues.
Respond using protocol: fix signals, assess the patient, and escalate when required.
Separate urgent patient-care issues from routine technical problems.
Document event timing, patient response, and technologist actions clearly.
Keep the record clean enough that scorers and providers can trust it later.
tasks.nextAction: Study artifact, signal loss, equipment problems, abnormal events, calibrations, and what must be documented.

tasks.title: Score adult studies
tasks.focus: Apply adult scoring rules accurately and consistently across sleep stages, arousals, respiratory events, movements, and cardiac findings.
studyTargets: Score with the correct adult staging and event rules.
Separate obstructive, central, mixed, hypoventilation, and hypoxemia concepts correctly.
Watch thresholds carefully and avoid overcalling artifact as scored data.
Use source standards when the distinction is subtle or version-sensitive.
Think accuracy first: staging, then events, then totals and indexes.
tasks.nextAction: Study adult staging, arousals, respiratory events, desaturations, movements, and cardiac annotations.

tasks.title: Score pediatric and infant studies
tasks.focus: Use pediatric and infant scoring logic carefully, especially when thresholds and normal patterns differ from adults.
studyTargets: Know that normal breathing, arousals, and CO2 expectations differ in children and infants.
Use pediatric rules for events, hypoventilation, and stage-specific interpretation where required.
Be careful with age-based norms and developmental issues.
Do not force adult assumptions onto pediatric studies.
Document anything age-specific that affects interpretation.
tasks.nextAction: Review pediatric/infant scoring differences, especially respiratory duration rules, CO2/hypoventilation, and age-related patterns.

tasks.title: Generate and verify report
tasks.focus: Turn scored findings into a clean, internally consistent report with correct summaries, indexes, and supporting graphics.
studyTargets: Check totals, indexes, and time-based calculations before finalizing anything.
Use the right terms for AHI, RDI, REI, sleep efficiency, latency, arousal data, and desaturation summaries.
Make sure narrative statements match the scored data.
Verify graphs, tables, and summary fields for internal consistency.
A report should be accurate, readable, and easy for the interpreting provider to trust.
tasks.nextAction: Practice calculations, report verification, indices, technologist notes, graphic summaries, and interpretation traps.

tasks.title: Administer PAP therapy
tasks.focus: Recognize when PAP is being applied correctly, when it needs adjustment, and when the patient is not tolerating it well.
studyTargets: Know basic PAP modes and when the setup appears to fit the order and study goals.
Watch for leak, poor seal, pressure intolerance, emergent central events, and comfort problems.
Support the patient while also preserving study quality.
Document pressure changes, interface issues, and response patterns clearly.
Stay at RPSGT depth: recognition, support, and protocol-based response.
tasks.nextAction: Study PAP modes, pressure changes, leak/interface troubleshooting, acclimation, and safety cues.

tasks.title: Identify alternative therapies
tasks.focus: Recognize non-PAP therapy pathways and when the record or patient history points toward them.
studyTargets: Know common alternatives such as oral appliance therapy, positional therapy, surgery, weight management, and selected device-based options.
Understand follow-up study use after non-PAP interventions at a technologist-recognition level.
Recognize when intolerance, anatomy, or patient preference may connect to alternatives.
Document relevant observations that support future treatment decisions.
Keep this at recognition level rather than advanced prescriptive management.
tasks.nextAction: Review oral appliances, positional therapy, surgery/upper-airway stimulation awareness, and candidate/caution clues.

tasks.title: Administer oxygen therapy
tasks.focus: Recognize oxygen-related orders, monitoring needs, and response patterns while following safety and protocol rules.
studyTargets: Know when oxygen is part of the study plan and how it affects monitoring and documentation.
Watch saturation trends, delivery changes, and interactions with respiratory events.
Document flow, timing, response, and any safety concerns clearly.
Do not confuse oxygen support with treatment of the underlying event type.
Stay alert for cases where oxygen, PAP, and hypoventilation monitoring interact.
tasks.nextAction: Study when oxygen is added, how it is titrated, and why ventilation/CO2 risk matters.
